candidates.changed_node: A's TS_MIN($low,21)/($close+eps) ratio replaced by TS_MIN($low,21)/(TS_MAX($high,21)+eps)
candidates.rationale: A's grandparent is B (693246746bbdc073 sits between them), so A already carries TS_MIN($low,21) donated from B; reusing just that would be cosmetic. The genuine new contribution is B's other extremum, TS_MAX($high,21), never seen anywhere in A's lineage. Swapping A's close-normalised floor ratio for a floor/ceiling ratio turns the leg into a range-compression measure (how tight the 21-day range has been) instead of a level ratio, which conditions the efficiency-gated reversal on realised range width -- a name pulling back to its floor inside a compressed range is a different animal from one doing so in a wide, choppy range, and neither parent alone can tell those apart. TS_MEAN($return,5) and the asset_turnover gate are kept verbatim from A.

A ranks EPS scaled by its own liquidity with zero price-location context; B ranks where close sits in its 21-day range with zero fundamental content. The product keeps both complete and creates a genuine interaction: a liquid, cheap-on-EPS name scores highest when it is also high in its own range -- the market actively re-rating a value name -- versus the same liquid-value name sitting at its floor (not yet recognised) or one whose range has already closed (fully priced). Neither parent alone can separate 'liquid value about to move' from 'liquid value dead in the range.'

candidates.changed_node: B multiplied into A's CS_ZSCORE(dollar_volume) leg, not appended as an independent third term
candidates.rationale: A's liquidity penalty (dollar-volume z-score subtracted from an EPS rank, rewarding under-the-radar profitable names) can't distinguish a genuine liquidity pickup from noise. Multiplying that penalty by B's range position turns raw volume into 'volume with price follow-through': the penalty bites hardest when heavy trading coincides with price sitting high in its range (confirmed attention) and is muted when volume is elevated but price is still at the floor (a spike without markup). B is grafted onto A's existing liquidity leg rather than added as a new rank term, deliberately avoiding the additive third-leg pattern that has failed to decorrelate elsewhere in this archive -- this stays a two-leg spread.

candidates.changed_node: B's TS_MEAN($return,10)*ABS($return) leg replaced by CS_RANK(A, whole)
candidates.rationale: B's momentum-magnitude-torque leg (mean return times its own absolute value, a generic volatility-event filter) is swapped for A's range position, keeping B's EPS-times-liquidity-rank leg intact. This changes the reference point from 'has the stock made a big move recently' to 'is the stock already high in its own 21-day channel' -- a slow, low-volatility grind to the top of the range now suppresses the value-liquidity signal exactly as a violent one-day spike would have in B, which neither parent expresses (A has no fundamental content, B's torque leg is direction- and level-blind).

candidates.changed_node: B's torque leg dropped (not replaced); B (range-position) used as a raw multiplicative weight instead of a ranked subtrahend
candidates.rationale: Same parent pair as pair 4 but a different fusion in kind, not degree: instead of substituting into A's spread, this keeps only A's EPS-times-liquidity-rank leg and uses B as a continuous amplitude conditioner -- the value-liquidity signal scales up when the name is high in its range and toward zero at the floor, rather than being netted against it as a ranked spread. Raw B and CS_RANK(B) enter in structurally different roles (multiplier vs. subtrahend), so despite sharing the donated EPS*liquidity-rank fragment with pair 4, the two children encode different economic bets and should not be read as duplicates.

candidates.changed_node: added CS_RANK((TS_MAX($high,21)-$close)/($close+eps)) ceiling-distance term, multiplied onto B
candidates.rationale: B is itself a child of A (it already inherited TS_MIN($low,21) from A), so reusing that fragment alone would be cosmetic. The fresh contribution is A's other extremum, TS_MAX($high,21), which B has never seen: turned into a price-normalised distance-to-ceiling rank and multiplied onto B's existing floor-relative-earnings-yield-vs-momentum spread. Economically: a name that screens cheap against its own low and hasn't already reversed is a stronger opportunity when it also has real room below its own high -- room to run that a pure floor-relative measure can't see, since B never looks at the ceiling.

A's floor-relative earnings-yield-vs-momentum spread has no notion of earnings quality; B's accrual-gap-times-volume-ratio flags exactly that -- aggressive accruals paired with a pickup in short-vs-long volume, read as informed skepticism reaching the tape. The product gates A's value signal by B's quality-and-attention check: a stock screening cheap-and-not-yet-reversed is credible only if it isn't also showing the volume signature of distribution in a low-quality-earnings name. Both parents already sit at depth 5 individually, so a top-level product is the only way to keep each completely intact within the depth-6 limit; the interaction (value confirmed by clean accruals) is what neither parent expresses alone.

B is a bare profitability level with no timing dynamic; A is a timing/skepticism signal (accrual quality times a volume-acceleration ratio) with no absolute-quality anchor. The product conditions A's accrual-and-volume warning on where the firm sits in absolute ROA terms: the same red flag is more credible in an already-low-ROA name (weak fundamentals plus a volume signature of distribution) than in a high-ROA name, where an accrual blip is more likely noise around a fundamentally strong business. B is only 2 nodes total (RANK($roa)) and is kept whole -- there is no larger complete sub-expression this parent can donate.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.
